newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Five groups fail to qualify for Brazil B Band bid.
newsitem.headline: Five groups fail to qualify for Brazil B Band bid.

text.p: Five consortia out of a total of 15 failed to qualify for bidding to operate any of Brazil's planned Band B cellular concessions, an official said.
The official said the consortia failed to qualify for various reasons, mainly by not providing sufficient financial guarantees or not proving their members had legally formed a consortium.
In one case, a group was disqualified for not using an official Brazilian translator for a document.
-- Lightel, comprised of private telecom operator Lightel, construction firm Queirroz Galvao (both from Brazil), and Korean Mobile Telecom. The group had presented bids for areas 5, 6 and 10.
-- Algar, comprised of the same members as Lightel. The group presented a bid for area 3.
-- Hutchison/Cowan, made up of telecommunications group Hutchinson Whampoa from Hong Kong and Brazilian construction company Cowan Construtora, which offered bids for areas 4 and 5.
-- Tess, comprised of Swedish telecom operator Telia, Brazil's Airline Cellular, and Primave, part of Brazilian construction group C.R. Alameida, which made bids for areas 1-6, 9-10.
